note: 2026-09-06 daily batch, written and pushed by the chairman BEFORE any seat was convened, so that every forecast in it is pre-registered rather than fitted; commit order proves the ordering and nothing else. THIS BATCH DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RUN YESTERDAY'S NEXT STEP 1 AS WRITTEN, BECAUSE THE RECORD ALREADY CONTAINS ITS ANSWER TWICE AND YESTERDAY'S COUNCIL DID NOT SEE IT. Next step 1 asked for 'two reads of UNCT/20/6 in ONE batch' to test for a per-request rotating field. The 2026-09-05 batch ALREADY CONTAINED THREE such reads - rows 1, 2 and 3 were the same URL with three different find strings, and scripts/fetch_relay.py fetch_one calls polite_get(url) once per row with no cache and no reuse, so each row is an independent HTTP fetch. Both committed runs of that batch carry three identical hashes within the run: blob 0824d1a4 (fetched_at 2026-09-05T11:14:48Z) rows 1-3 all sha256 c167c772f53ef32f at 105703 bytes, and blob ba90749f (fetched_at 2026-09-05T12:18:41Z) rows 1-3 likewise all c167c772f53ef32f at 105703 bytes. PER-REQUEST ROTATION IS FALSIFIED SIX TIMES OVER, IN ONE RUN AND ACROSS TWO, AND THE SECOND ADDENDUM REACHED FOR THE 64-MINUTE CROSS-RUN PAIR WHEN THE ZERO-ELAPSED SAME-BATCH TRIPLE WAS SITTING IN THE SAME FILE. Today's batch therefore spends no row re-running a settled test and spends them on the half that is genuinely open. PURPOSE 1 - SEPARATE A DAILY-ROTATING FIELD FROM A REAL CONTENT CHANGE, WHICH IS THE ONLY LIVE HALF OF NEXT STEP 1. The second addendum states the remaining ambiguity exactly: a field rotating once per day - a build hash, a cache stamp, a date string - fits every observation as well as a real change does, and two reads 64 minutes apart cannot separate them. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A CONTROL SET, NOT A REPEAT READ. The 2026-09-05 batch read SIX icsid.worldbank.org case-detail pages at 200 and committed a hash for each. If the host stamps its case-detail pages with anything that rotates daily, ALL SIX hashes move today. If none moves, there is no daily stamp on this surface and the 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-05 change on UNCT/20/6 was a real content change. BASELINE, cited by blob and not by path because the path is overwritten in place (0903-B6), all from reduction blob ba90749f2b0f6f33757907993bab1cb32c5fd2ed, request 2026-09-05-daily.json, fetched_at 2026-09-05T12:18:41.387430+00:00, control_ok true, void false: UNCT/20/6 = 105703 bytes / c167c772f53ef32f; ARB/22/2 = 94751 / 9f197f396c34d838; ARB/22/30 = 95712 / ae24da73b61ade61; ARB/24/18 = 93692 / 6d8440a5bf44bd85; ARB/24/26 = 86797 / ce4b5d8537c3f68b; ARB/24/46 = 88573 / d56a44f424ae2cef. THE FOUR-BRANCH DECISION RULE IS PRE-REGISTERED HERE AND IN analytics/daily-research/2026-09-06.md Part I section 5, WRITTEN BEFORE ANY ANSWER EXISTS, AND IT BINDS EVERY SEAT TODAY. It is graded on the sha256 fields of rows 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 against those six baselines. BRANCH 1 - all six unchanged: there is no daily-rotating field on this host's case-detail pages, the 09-04 to 09-05 UNCT/20/6 change was a real content change, and sha256 is a sound change detector on this surface. BRANCH 2 - all six changed: consistent with a host-wide daily stamp, and the 09-04 to 09-05 UNCT/20/6 delta is NOT evidence that anything substantive moved. BRANCH 3 - UNCT/20/6 changed and all five ARB pages unchanged: the change is page-specific and not a host stamp; this licenses 'something in the bytes of the UNCT/20/6 page moved between 09-05 and 09-06' and NOTHING WHATEVER about what moved or whether it is substantive. BRANCH 4 - any other pattern, including some ARB pages moving and others not: NO BRANCH IS ENTERED, the result is reported as unresolved, and no seat may fit a story to it. NO BRANCH SAYS ANYTHING ABOUT ANY CASE. A hash is a fact about bytes and a byte count is a fact about a fetch. FORECAST A, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 1: the 400-character 'Status of Proceeding' window on UNCT/20/6 returns CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to 'dent(s): Trade Law Bureau, Global Affairs Canada, Ottawa, Canada Language(s) of Proceeding: English Status of Proceeding: Pending Latest Development: December 2, 2025 - Each party files a statement of costs. (a) Original Proceeding Published Decisions Witness Statement of Theodore David Einarsson (Public Version) Procedural Order Statement of Defence Confidentiality Order Witness Statement of Russ'. FORECAST B, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 2: the 400-character 'Subject of Dispute' window on UNCT/20/6 returns CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to 'CT/20/6) Proceeding Materials Procedural Details Proceeding Proceeding Materials Procedural Details Subject of Dispute: Seismic data enterprise Economic Sector: Other Industry Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement) Applicable Rules: UNCITRAL (a) Original Proceeding Claimant(s)/Nationality(ies): (i) Theodore David Einarsson (U.S.), Harold Paul Einarsson (U.S.), Russe'. DISCLOSED NON-INDEPENDENCE, in advance: rows 1 and 2 are two of the six hash rows AND they carry forecasts A and B. A window can return character-identical while the page hash moves, because the window is 400 characters of a 105703-byte body. Forecasts A and B and the hash branches are therefore NOT independent confirmations of each other and may not be counted as such; the interesting cell is precisely A and B confirmed WITH the hash moved, which would locate the change outside both windows and is the strongest single row-pair this batch can produce. PURPOSE 2 - A FIFTH OBSERVATION OF THE www.iisd.org REFUSAL, at one row. FORECAST C, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 8: https://www.iisd.org/itn/feed/ returns a NON-200. Four observations stand - 2026-09-04 at 11:50:42Z and 12:48:31Z, 2026-09-05 at 11:14:48Z and 12:18:41Z - all with good controls. This row costs one slot and it is the cheapest thing that can falsify escalation 2's premise before Monday's collection grades it. IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE FETCH LAYER AND ABOUT NOTHING ELSE. The Grosse Ruse-Khan article is NOT re-fired: three refusals is enough, its gap slug grosse-ruse-khan-itn-ip-isds-plain-packaging-to-patent-revocation stays open, no seat has read that body, and nothing may be asserted from its title or from a status code. PURPOSE 3 - RESOLVE WHETHER THE ICSID CASE-DETAIL CHANNEL IS AN INTAKE CHANNEL (next step 4). Yesterday's close-out named the bottleneck: this council can VERIFY any docket it can NAME and cannot DISCOVER one it cannot. specs/icsid.yaml lines 11-13 say the case database at https://icsid.worldbank.org/cases/case-database is JS-RENDERED, that a polite GET returns only an app shell with a 'Search Cases' heading and NO case data in raw HTML, and that no public RSS or JSON case endpoint was found; its warnings block records that an internal JSON API the SPA calls was NOT investigated. THE RELAY HAS FIRED AT THAT URL EXACTLY ONCE, AND I FOUND IT BY SCREENING RATHER THAN BY REMEMBERING - I had drafted the sentence 'no seat has ever fired the relay at that URL' and my own entry-28 screen falsified it before this file was pushed. Instrument: python over every committed blob at analytics/fetch-results/*.json, enumerated with git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only and NO path argument, at commit 99d3624; 48 reduction files; known-positive control on the same sweep found 101 example.com rows, so the sweep finds what is there. THE ONE PRIOR ROW: analytics/fetch-results/2026-08-24-zz-subject-of-dispute.json, fetched_at 2026-08-24T12:51:47.711402+00:00, control_ok true - https://icsid.worldbank.org/cases/case-database returned outcome ok, status 200, 75571 bytes, sha256 5927a1aa6e57089c, find 'Subject of Dispute', find_matched FALSE with an EMPTY excerpt. That row is consistent with the spec and it tested neither literal that would settle the question: it never asked whether the app shell is there, and it never asked whether ANY case identifier is in the raw body. Rows 9 and 10 ask exactly those, and the 75571-byte / 5927a1aa6e57089c pair from thirteen days ago is a free seventh baseline for purpose 1 on a NON-case-detail page of the same host. Rows 9, 10 and 11 test the spec's claim directly. FORECAST D, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 9: /cases/case-database returns outcome 'ok' with status 200 and find_matched true for 'Search Cases'. FORECAST E, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 10: the same URL with find 'ARB/' returns find_matched FALSE, confirming the spec - no case identifier is present in the raw body. FORECAST G, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROWS 9 AND 10 TOGETHER: both rows return 75571 bytes and sha256 5927a1aa6e57089c, unchanged from 2026-08-24. If this page is byte-identical across thirteen days while the case-detail pages move, that is strong evidence against any host-wide rotating stamp, and it is purpose 1's longest lever. FORECAST F, FALSIFIABLE, GRADED ON ROW 11: https://icsid.worldbank.org/news-events, the documented static fallback, returns outcome 'ok' with status 200 and find_matched true for 'ICSID'. BINDING READING RULE ON ROWS 9 TO 11, AND IT IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE BROKEN TODAY: these are CHANNEL DIAGNOSTICS, not discovery. METHODOLOGY Part VIII makes the relay a retrieval channel for what the sources or the record already identified. NO case number, case name, party or matter appearing in any excerpt returned by rows 9, 10 or 11 may be entered into this record as a discovered matter, screened, graded on any ring, or carried as a lead today. If forecast E is FALSIFIED - if case identifiers do appear in the raw body - that is a fact about the CHANNEL and about the accuracy of specs/icsid.yaml, it goes to Emory as a PROPOSAL, and this council builds nothing: the source_analytics patch, the health column, the polite_get diagnostic CLI, the IAReporter feed swap, the Kluwer source, the category signal, the build_graph fix and any ledger amendment are on the operator's pending list and stay zero-budget. ARB/23/3 IS DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED: its 'No References Available.' resolution may not be revived without first addressing the ICSID register's Decision on Preliminary Objections of 21 December 2023, and a status row today would invite exactly that. ARB/12/1 IS DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED: the 2026-09-03 close-out ruled this council off the character-geometry programme and that ruling stands. Row 12 is a TAIL CONTROL; with the relay's prepended head control it establishes the instrument was live at both ends of the run. STANDING READING RULES, restated because they are the ones this council keeps having to re-learn: a returned excerpt establishes what its own 400 characters contain and NOTHING about what lies outside them; an absent literal establishes that excerpt_of found no match on the returned body - A STATEMENT ABOUT THE FETCH, NOT ABOUT THE DOCKET; a 404 or non-200 is information about the URL pattern, NEVER about the case; every count derived from this reduction must carry its COMMIT as well as its scope (0903-B2); and an unqualified claim about 'the tree' is enumerated with git ls-tree -r <commit> and no path argument (entry 29, binding from today). MAX_URLS is 12 and it truncates REQUESTED rows BEFORE the control is prepended (scripts/fetch_relay.py lines 195-197). THIS BATCH REQUESTS EXACTLY 12 ROWS, so nothing is truncated and the reduction should carry 13 records: the prepended head control, then rows 1-12 in the order listed. A reduction with 'truncated': true, or with any count other than requested 12, is an instrument discrepancy and must be reported as one before any row is read. Note that 'completed' counts only outcome=='ok' rows, so a CONFIRMED forecast C makes completed 11 rather than 12 BY DESIGN and that is not a discrepancy.
